mainEntity.name: What is the difference between PRF and PRP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both come from your own blood, but PRF (Platelet-Rich Fibrin) is centrifuged at lower speeds with no anticoagulants, producing a fibrin scaffold that traps platelets and releases growth factors gradually over days. PRP releases growth factors more quickly. For the under-eye area, the sustained release of PRF is often preferred for skin quality.

mainEntity.name: Will it remove dark circles completely?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the cause. Dark circles from thin or compromised skin quality respond well to PRF over a series of sessions. Dark circles from deeper pigment, vascular shadows or hollows often need a combined plan — PRF plus filler, or PRF plus a targeted brightening protocol. We diagnose the type in consultation.

Skin-quality changes from PRF typically last 9 to 12 months. We recommend a touch-up session at that interval to maintain the result. The under-eye area continues to age over time, so periodic maintenance preserves the improvement.

hero.title: PRF Under Eyes in Miami
hero.lede: Platelet-Rich Fibrin prepared from the patient's own blood is injected into the delicate under-eye area to release growth factors slowly over time, improving dark circles, fine lines and skin quality.

blocks.title: What it does for you
list: Improves tone and texture of the under-eye area using the patient's own biological growth factors.
Softens fine lines and crepiness around the eye contour.
Reduces appearance of dark circles caused by thin or compromised skin quality.
100% autologous — only the patient's own platelet-rich fibrin is used.
PRF (vs. PRP) releases growth factors more slowly thanks to its fibrin matrix, sustaining the regenerative effect.
Protocol typically 2–3 sessions spaced 4 weeks apart, then maintenance every 6–12 months.
